learning_objective: See that doubling a 3-4-5 triangle gives 6² + 8² = 10² by counting unit squares.

beats.name: triangle
beats.description: Draw the right triangle and its side lengths
beats.caption: A right triangle with legs 6 and 8
beats.narration: Here is a right triangle with legs 6 and 8 and hypotenuse 10.

beats.name: square_a
beats.description: Square on leg a, as a grid of unit cells
beats.caption: Leg 6: square of area 6² = 36
beats.narration: The square on the leg of length 6 holds 36 unit squares.

beats.name: square_b
beats.description: Square on leg b, as a grid of unit cells
beats.caption: Leg 8: square of area 8² = 64
beats.narration: The square on the leg of length 8 holds 64 unit squares.

beats.name: square_c
beats.description: Square on the hypotenuse, as a grid of unit cells
beats.caption: Hypotenuse 10: area 10² = 100
beats.narration: The square on the hypotenuse, of length 10, holds 100 unit squares.

beats.name: equation
beats.caption: The two smaller areas add up to the largest
beats.narration: Add the two smaller areas: 36 plus 64 is 100.

beats.name: hold
beats.caption: So 6² + 8² = 10²
beats.narration: So 6 squared plus 8 squared equals 10 squared.
